<description>
When starting a node with pruning enabled (e.g. `-prune=550`) on a node with full chain history or pruning many files at once, `FindFilesToPrune` and `FindFilesToPruneManual` previously called `PruneOneBlockFile` once per file.

Because `PruneOneBlockFile` iterated over the entire `m_block_index` for each file, this was an O(M * N) operation (M = files to prune, N = total blocks). When pruning a full chain (~5,770 files and ~972k blocks), this triggered ~5.6 billion iterations and froze the node running on a Pi 5 for ~10 minutes on startup while holding `cs_main`.

This PR replaces `PruneOneBlockFile` with `PruneBlockFiles(const std::set<int>&)`, which collects all candidate files and prunes them in a single O(M + N) pass over `m_block_index` using a compact dynamic `bitfield (std::vector<bool>)`. Also skips entries without block or undo data to avoid unneeded checks and prevent file 0 pruning from dirtying header-only or already-pruned index entries. The new signature is analogous to `UnlinkPrunedFiles({file_number});`.

Benchmarked with ~972k blocks and 5,770 files to prune:
- x86_64 (i7-8665U @ 1.90 GHz): 75.1s -> 14.7ms (~5,100x speedup)
- ARM64 (Raspberry Pi 5): 606.0s -> 26.3ms (>3,500x speedup)

Add unit test `blockmanager_prune_block_files_batch` to verify batch pruning, empty set no-ops, and clean dirty-set behavior. Update caller tests in `blockmanager_tests` and `rescan_tests`.
</description>
